q: What energy efficiency loans does SIDBI offer MSMEs?
title: SIDBI energy efficiency loans for MSMEs
short: SIDBI's main route is the 4E scheme, End to End Energy Efficiency: an energy audit, a project report and help with implementation, followed by a loan for the measures the audit recommends. SIDBI has also run the Partial Risk Sharing Facility, which guarantees part of other lenders' energy efficiency loans. Terms change, so confirm with SIDBI.

p: 4E pairs technical help with a direct SIDBI loan. The usual sequence is a walk-through audit, a detailed energy audit, a bankable project report, implementation support, and then finance for the measures the audit identified, such as efficient motors, compressors, furnaces or waste heat recovery. Ask SIDBI for the current minimum loan, rate and margin, as these are set in its scheme terms and revised from time to time.

The Partial Risk Sharing Facility for Energy Efficiency, PRSF, was set up with World Bank and Global Environment Facility support and run by SIDBI. It does not lend to you. It covers part of the loss a participating bank or NBFC would take on an energy efficiency loan, often one made through an energy service company. Programmes like this open and close as funding rounds end, so ask which ones are taking new projects.

ADEETIE is a BEE scheme, not a SIDBI loan. It pays interest subvention, 5 percent for micro and small and 3 percent for medium enterprises, on loans for energy-efficient technology from participating lenders, in notified clusters. A unit may be able to combine an audit under one programme with finance from another; check each scheme's rules before assuming they stack.

sections.h: What to have ready before you apply
ul: Twelve months of electricity bills and fuel invoices, to set the baseline.
Production records for the same months, so savings can be shown per tonne or per unit.
Quotations for the equipment and the expected energy saving from an auditor.
Udyam registration and the usual financial documents your lender asks for.

senseible: Senseible's green loan readiness check organises the energy and emissions evidence lenders ask for, from your bills and invoices. It does not arrange SIDBI loans or confirm scheme eligibility.
